title: Model Release Notes (Customer-Safe) — Style Guide
author: Elliot Price
content:
h1. Purpose
This page defines how Redwood Inference writes *customer-visible* model release notes (the “model changelog”). The goal is to be transparent and useful for production engineering teams while ensuring we *do not leak internal-only details* (vendors, incident context, infrastructure specifics, internal codenames, or security-sensitive information).

This guide applies to:
- Auto-generated release notes produced by the changelog generator
- Human edits during review/approval
- Manual hotfix corrections and “superseding” entries

Non-goals:
- Writing long narratives about quality changes (v1 only links/metrics; no speculative explanations)
- Sharing internal evaluation prompts, customer-specific details, or incident RCA content

h1. Audience and tone
*Audience:* ML engineers, platform engineers, and engineering managers running production inference.

*Tone principles:*
- Be direct, factual, and brief.
- Prefer “what changed” and “what should I do” over “why we did it”.
- Use consistent terminology across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
- If impact is unknown or workload-dependent, say so explicitly.

h1. Release note taxonomy (customer-visible)
Every entry must select one primary type (used for filtering in Console/docs/feed):
1. *New model version* (availability + compatibility)
2. *Behavior/quality change* (only when backed by eval links/metrics)
3. *Performance/latency change* (throughput, P50/P95; can be “no change observed”)
4. *Compatibility change* (API parameters, tool/function calling, context window, structured output)
5. *Safety/policy update* (policy alignment, refusal behavior adjustments; no internal rule dumps)
6. *Bug fix* (serving/runtime integration issues affecting outputs or stability)
7. *Deprecation notice* (timeline + migration guidance)
8. *Operational correction* (superseding/clarifying a previously published note)

If multiple changes apply, choose the primary type and list the rest under “Other changes”.

h1. Required sections (MUST include)
All customer-visible notes must include the following sections, in this order.

h2. 1) Summary (2–4 sentences)
- State model + version
- One-sentence description of the change
- Who is affected (if scoped)

h2. 2) Impact
- Describe customer-observable impact (behavior, cost, latency, stability)
- Include clear action guidance:
  - “No action required” or
  - “Pin to version X” / “Test before rollout” / “Update parameter usage”

h2. 3) Compatibility
*Always present,* even if “no change”. Include:
- API surface: supported endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank), streaming, structured output
- Tool/function calling: supported/unchanged/limited
- Context window / max output tokens (if relevant)
- Parameter compatibility notes (e.g., unchanged semantics; or specify changes)

h2. 4) Availability / rollout
Clarify where/when the version is available:
- Hosted: region availability + rollout status (e.g., “GA”, “phased rollout”, “by-request”)
- Dedicated: whether new deployments default to this version; whether existing clusters require opt-in
- Private: minimum platform/runtime versions (if applicable) and upgrade guidance

h2. 5) Links
Include at least one of the following, as applicable:
- Console model/version page (canonical)
- Public changelog permalink
- Evaluation dashboard link (when claiming behavior/quality changes)
- Performance dashboard link (when claiming perf changes)

If a link is not available, write: “Links: Not available for this entry” and explain why (e.g., “historical entry pre-migration”).

h2. 6) Deprecation (conditional but standardized)
If this entry is a deprecation (or references one), include:
- What is being deprecated (model/version)
- Sunset date (YYYY-MM-DD) and any phases (see template below)
- Recommended replacement(s)
- What happens at sunset (requests rejected vs mapped to replacement vs require pin)

h1. Optional sections (include when relevant)
- *Performance* (P50/P95 latency, throughput, token/s, cost per 1M tokens): keep numbers scoped and comparable.
- *Safety & policy notes:* describe category-level change; do not expose internal policy tags.
- *Known issues / limitations:* only customer-actionable; include workaround if available.
- *Migration notes:* only if action required; keep to 3–6 bullets.
- *Other changes:* small bullet list.

h1. Language: DO / DON’T
h2. DO
- Use “*Model version*” and “*version ID*” consistently.
- Use specific, actionable phrasing:
  - “If you require stable outputs for compliance sign-off, pin to {version_id} and subscribe to the feed.”
  - “Tool calling is supported; JSON schema mode is unchanged.”
- When reporting performance changes, specify scope and measurement context:
  - “Measured on Hosted us-east-1, streaming enabled, 1–4k prompt tokens; your results may vary.”
- State uncertainty explicitly:
  - “We did not observe statistically significant changes on our standard eval set; customer workloads may vary.”

h2. DON’T
- Don’t mention internal codenames, model nicknames, or vendor contract details.
- Don’t mention underlying hardware SKU, kernel names, compilation strategies, or internal routing policies.
- Don’t mention incident ticket numbers, on-call rotations, or customer account names.
- Don’t claim quality improvements without a link to an evaluation dashboard or published metric.
- Don’t include exact abuse strings, safety triggers, or policy bypass details.

h1. Prohibited internal details (redaction requirements)
The following must *never* appear in customer-visible notes:
- Internal model aliases/codenames (e.g., “rwi-<internal>”, “project <name>”)
- Raw registry fields marked internal-only (anything not in the public allowlist)
- Vendor or partner names when under NDA, or sourcing/procurement details
- Hardware specifics (GPU model, stepping, interconnect), kernel names, attention implementation names, compiler flags
- Internal routing rules (priority tiers, fallback policies by account, region strategy details)
- Security-sensitive data:
  - exact safety classifier thresholds
  - exploit details or reproduction steps that increase risk
- Customer identifiers:
  - account names, deployment IDs, contract tier specifics, support ticket IDs

If a release note draft contains any prohibited detail, send it back to “Draft” and request re-rendering/redaction.

h1. Formatting rules
- Dates must be ISO: YYYY-MM-DD.
- Use short paragraphs; prefer bullets for action items.
- Avoid ambiguous terms: “soon”, “later”, “recently”, “minor”. Replace with a date, phase, or measurable statement.
- Use consistent capitalization:
  - Hosted, Dedicated, Private, Console
  - model_id, version_id
- If referencing parameters, show them as code: `max_output_tokens`, `response_format`, `tool_choice`.

h1. Templates
Below are approved templates. The generator should produce one of these, and reviewers should keep edits within these structures.

h2. Template A — New model version (GA)
*Summary*
- {model_display_name} ({model_id}) — New version {version_id} is now available.

*Impact*
- No action required for existing pinned integrations.
- If you are not pinning versions, your traffic may gradually shift to {version_id} as part of standard rollout.

*Compatibility*
- Endpoints: {endpoints}
- Tool/function calling: {supported/notes}
- Context window: {n_tokens}
- Structured output: {supported/notes}

*Availability / rollout*
- Hosted: {regions} — {GA/phased} starting {date}
- Dedicated: {default/opt-in} (contact Support for scheduling if you require a change window)
- Private: available starting Redwood Private {min_version} (or “not applicable”)

*Links*
- Console: {console_url}
- Changelog permalink: {changelog_url}

h2. Template B — Performance/latency update
*Summary*
- {model_display_name} {version_id} — Performance update.

*Impact*
- Expected impact: {latency/throughput/cost direction} for {scope}.
- Action: {no action / consider re-benchmarking / contact us if SLO regression}

*Compatibility*
- No API changes.
- Tool/function calling: unchanged.

*Performance*
- Observed change (Hosted reference): {metric statement}
- Scope: {regions/routes/settings}

*Availability / rollout*
- Hosted: effective {date}
- Dedicated/Private: {notes}

*Links*
- Performance dashboard: {perf_url}
- Console: {console_url}

h2. Template C — Compatibility change (customer action required)
*Summary*
- {model_display_name} {version_id} — Compatibility update.

*Impact*
- Action required: {what to change} by {date/phase}.

*Compatibility*
- Changed: {bullet list}
- Unchanged: {bullet list}

*Migration notes*
1. {step}
2. {step}
3. {step}

*Availability / rollout*
- Hosted: {phased/GA}
- Dedicated/Private: {minimum versions / upgrade requirements}

*Links*
- Console: {console_url}
- Docs: {docs_url}

h2. Template D — Deprecation notice
*Summary*
- Deprecation: {model_display_name} {version_id or model_id}.

*Impact*
- Action required: migrate to {replacement_model/version}.

*Deprecation timeline*
- Phase 1 (notice): {YYYY-MM-DD}
- Phase 2 (no new deployments / limited availability): {YYYY-MM-DD}
- Phase 3 (sunset): {YYYY-MM-DD}

*What happens at sunset*
- Hosted: {reject / map to replacement / requires pin}
- Dedicated: {support window details}
- Private: {support window details}

*Migration notes*
- Recommended replacement: {replacement}
- Compatibility considerations: {bullets}

*Links*
- Console: {console_url}
- Changelog permalink: {changelog_url}

h2. Template E — Operational correction (superseding)
*Summary*
- Correction: This entry supersedes release note {previous_entry_id} published on {date}.

*What changed*
- {one paragraph explanation of the correction}

*Customer impact*
- {explicitly state if guidance changed}

*Links*
- Original entry: {url}
- Updated entry: {url}

h1. Claims policy (quality, safety, and performance)
h2. Quality/behavior claims
You may say:
- “We observed improvements on Redwood’s standard eval set” *only if* you include an eval link and name the metric family (e.g., “tool-call success rate”, “format adherence”).

You may not say:
- “Better reasoning” / “more accurate” / “more aligned” without metrics.

Approved phrasing examples:
- “On Redwood’s public tool-calling eval suite, tool-call success rate increased from 86% to 90% for the tested configuration. See eval link.”
- “We did not observe significant changes on Redwood’s standard regression set; customer workloads may vary.”

h2. Safety/policy claims
Allowed:
- “Updated refusal behavior for disallowed content categories; no changes to allowed-use categories.”
- “Reduced false-positive refusals for benign medical information queries, based on internal policy testing.”

Not allowed:
- Specific detection triggers, bypass methods, or exact category rules beyond high-level descriptions.

h2. Performance claims
Required:
- Identify scope (Hosted region, streaming on/off, prompt length band).
- Prefer percent ranges over overly precise numbers unless strongly validated.

h1. Review checklist (for approvers)
Before moving an entry from “in_review” to “published”, confirm:
1. *Customer-safe:* no prohibited internal details.
2. *Completeness:* all required sections present (Summary, Impact, Compatibility, Availability, Links).
3. *Actionability:* Impact includes clear customer guidance.
4. *Compatibility clarity:* tool/function calling and context window explicitly stated.
5. *Deprecations:* timeline is explicit and consistent with policy.
6. *Links:* do not 404; correct model/version.
7. *Claims backed by evidence:* quality/perf claims include links.
8. *Language:* no speculation; no internal blame; no incident context.

h1. Examples (approved)
h2. Example 1 — Simple new version
Summary
- Redwood: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct — New version `llama-3.1-70b-instruct-2026-02-10` is now available.

Impact
- No action required. If you pin versions, your integration will remain on your pinned version.

Compatibility
- Endpoints: Chat Completions, Completions
- Tool/function calling: Supported (unchanged)
- Context window: 128k
- Structured output: Supported (unchanged)

Availability / rollout
- Hosted: phased rollout in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 starting 2026-02-10
- Dedicated: available for new deployments; opt-in for existing clusters

Links
- Console: https://console.redwoodinference.com/models/llama-3.1-70b-instruct/versions/llama-3.1-70b-instruct-2026-02-10
- Changelog permalink: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/model-release-notes/llama-3.1-70b-instruct#llama-3.1-70b-instruct-2026-02-10

h2. Example 2 — Deprecation
Summary
- Deprecation: `acme-embed-v2`.

Impact
- Action required: migrate to `acme-embed-v3` by 2026-05-01.

Deprecation timeline
- Phase 1 (notice): 2026-02-15
- Phase 2 (no new deployments): 2026-03-15
- Phase 3 (sunset): 2026-05-01

What happens at sunset
- Hosted: requests to `acme-embed-v2` will be rejected with a deprecation error.
- Dedicated/Private: contact Support to schedule a controlled migration window.

Links
- Console: https://console.redwoodinference.com/models/acme-embed-v2
- Migration guide: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/model-release-notes/acme-embed-v2#migrate

h1. Escalation and exceptions
- If a note may involve sensitive security context or policy nuance, request review from *Marcus Lin* (Security) and *Naomi Feldman* (Compliance) before publishing.
- If a note is driven by runtime-level changes that affect multiple models, coordinate with *Connor O’Brien* (Release Engineering) to cross-link runtime release notes, but keep model notes customer-safe.
- For urgent corrections: publish a superseding entry (Template E). Do not edit a published entry in-place without preserving history.

h1. Appendix: Common replacements for internal jargon
- “We changed kernel X / attention implementation Y” → “We updated the serving implementation to improve performance and stability.”
- “We moved you to a different cluster / region due to capacity” → “Availability updated; see rollout details.”
- “We changed routing policy / fallback rules” → “Improved reliability during capacity events; no API changes.”

h1. Doc ownership
- Owner: Developer Experience (Docs Site)
- Primary maintainer: Elliot Price
- Changes require review from: Docs (Wei Chen), Product (Marissa Cole), and at least one of Security/Compliance when relevant.
